answer.rationale: The proposal complies with all applicable standards. The data set is classified as C2 Confidential due to delivery addresses (DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1). Parcelytics' contract covers C2 data under its DPA (CT-PARCEL@v2) in compliance with SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1, and its US hosting region satisfies DRS-01@v1#DR-2 for US data subjects. Outbound traffic routes from zone Z2 through int-gw (NET-STD@v2#NZ-1, ADR-031@v1#D1). Data in transit uses mTLS (SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1), retention is 25 days which is under the 30-day limit (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1), and data is stored encrypted at rest (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2). The planned go live date of 2027-01-05 is outside the peak season freeze window ending 2027-01-04 (CHG-CAL@2026).

Proposal T01 complies with all applicable architecture, security, network, and data residency policies, and its planned go-live date falls outside the change freeze window. Under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 and DC-3.1, the integration is classified as C2 Confidential due to the inclusion of delivery addresses. Vendor contract CT-PARCEL@v2 includes a Data Processing Agreement covering C2 data (satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1) and hosts data in the US, satisfying DRS-01@v1#DR-2 since data subjects are located in the US (AX-EU@v1 is not applicable). Data in transit is secured using mutual TLS, meeting SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1. Data at rest is retained for 25 days (within the 30-day limit of SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1) and encrypted at rest, meeting SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2. Routing from network zone Z2 via int-gw complies with NET-STD@v2#NZ-1 and ADR-031@v1#D1; the egress proxy is not required as the service does not originate in Z3 (NET-STD@v2#NZ-2). Finally, the planned go-live of 2027-01-05 is outside the peak season freeze ending 2027-01-04 (CHG-CAL@2026). With zero violations and zero conditions, the proposal is approved pursuant to ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4.

The integration sends shipment IDs (C1) and delivery addresses (C2), making the overall classification C2 under DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1. All applicable rules are satisfied: Parcelytics's DPA in CT-PARCEL@v2 covers C1 and C2 data (SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1, SP-2.2); data in transit uses mutual TLS (SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1); retention is 25 days, within the 30-day limit (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1); data is encrypted at rest (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2); data subjects are in the US, so AX-EU@v1 does not apply and US hosting under CT-PARCEL@v2 satisfies DRS-01@v1#DR-2; the service is in Z2 and routes through int-gw without needing the Z3 egress proxy (NET-STD@v2#NZ-1, NZ-2; ADR-031@v1#D1); and the planned go-live date of 2027-01-05 is outside the peak season freeze window ending 2027-01-04 (CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1). With no violations and no conditions, the proposal is approved under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4.

Proposal T01 sends shipment IDs (C1) and delivery addresses (C2) to Parcelytics, classifying the integration as C2 Confidential under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 and DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1. Evaluating all applicable rules:

1. Vendor eligibility (SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1, SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.2): Under CT-PARCEL@v2, Parcelytics's data processing agreement covers C1 and C2 data, and no C3 data is sent.
2. Data residency and regional annexes (DRS-01@v1#DR-2, AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1): All data subjects are in the US, so AX-EU@v1 does not apply (ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.2). Under DRS-01@v1#DR-2, C2 data about US data subjects may be processed in any contracted region (US under CT-PARCEL@v2).
3. Data in transit (SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1): Data is transferred over mutual TLS (mTLS), satisfying the requirement for C2 data.
4. Data at rest and retention (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1, SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2): Parcelytics retains the data for 25 days (within the 30-day maximum) and stores it encrypted at rest.
5. Network zoning and routing (NET-STD@v2#NZ-1, NET-STD@v2#NZ-2, ADR-031@v1#D1): The sending service runs in Z2 and routes outbound vendor traffic through the integration gateway (int-gw). The egress proxy requirement in NET-STD@v2#NZ-2 applies only to Z3 services.
6. Change calendar (CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1): The planned production go-live date of 2027-01-05 falls after the peak season freeze window (2026-12-14 to 2027-01-04 inclusive).

Because there are no violations and no conditions, the proposal is approved under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4.

The payload contains delivery addresses (C2 personal data under DCS-01@v2), classifying the integration as C2 under DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1. Parcelytics has a valid DPA covering C2 under CT-PARCEL@v2, satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1. The 25-day retention period satisfies SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1 (with AX-EU@v1 not applying because subjects are US-based), encryption at rest satisfies SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2, US hosting satisfies DRS-01@v1#DR-2, and calling via int-gw from Z2 satisfies ADR-031@v1#D1 and NET-STD@v2#NZ-1. 

Two rules require conditions:
1. Standard HTTPS in place of mTLS fails SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1, but is covered by waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-07 because the planned go-live (2026-12-15) falls within the waiver window (ending 2026-12-31) and all data subjects are in the US. Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.2, SP-3.1 is recorded as a condition.
2. The planned go-live date of 2026-12-15 falls within the peak season freeze window (2026-12-14 to 2027-01-04). Under CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1 and ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.3, this must be rescheduled outside the freeze window and is recorded as a condition.

With zero violations and two conditions, the proposal is approved with conditions under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4.

The integration sends shipment IDs (C1) and delivery addresses (C2), giving the data set a classification of C2 Confidential under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 and DC-3.1. CT-PARCEL@v2 covers C1 and C2 data under its DPA (satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1) and hosts in the US (satisfying DRS-01@v1#DR-2 for US data subjects; AX-EU@v1 does not apply). The sending service resides in zone Z2 and routes through the integration gateway without needing the Z3 egress proxy, complying with NET-STD@v2#NZ-1 and ADR-031@v1#D1. Two conditions apply:

Standard HTTPS fails SP-3.1, but waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-07 covers Parcelytics for US data subjects through 2026-12-31, which encompasses the planned go-live date of 2026-12-15. 2. The planned production go-live of 2026-12-15 falls within the peak season freeze window (2026-12-14 to 2027-01-04). Under CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1 and ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.3, production go-live is approved only on condition that it moves outside the freeze window.

With zero violations and two conditions, the proposal is decided as approve_with_conditions per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4.

The integration sends shipment IDs (C1) and delivery addresses (C2), making the overall classification C2 under DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1. Parcelytics is eligible to receive C2 data under its DPA (CT-PARCEL@v2, SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1), and since all data subjects are in the US, its US hosting region satisfies DRS-01@v1#DR-2. Retention of 25 days and encryption at rest satisfy SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1 and SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2. Routing from zone Z2 through the integration gateway (int-gw) satisfies NET-STD@v2#NZ-1 and ADR-031@v1#D1 (the egress proxy rule NZ-2 applies only to Z3). However, using standard HTTPS for C2 data fails SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1. This failure is covered by waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-07 (which names SP-3.1 and vendor Parcelytics, covers only US data subjects, and is valid through 2026-12-31, covering the 2026-12-15 go-live date), resulting in a condition on SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1 per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.2. Additionally, the planned production go-live date of 2026-12-15 falls within the Peak season freeze window (2026-12-14 to 2027-01-04), resulting in a condition under CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1 and ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.3. With no violations and two conditions, the proposal is approved with conditions.

Under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 and DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1, the integration is classified as C2 because it includes delivery addresses (C2) alongside shipment IDs (C1). Per CT-PARCEL@v2, Parcelytics is contracted to process C1 and C2 data in the US hosting region, satisfying vendor eligibility (SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1, SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.2) and US data residency requirements (DRS-01@v1#DR-2). Because all data subjects are in the US, AX-EU@v1 does not apply. Retention of 25 days meets the 30-day maximum (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1), and data is encrypted at rest (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2). Network routing from zone Z2 through int-gw without the Z3 egress proxy satisfies NET-STD@v2#NZ-1, NET-STD@v2#NZ-2, and ADR-031@v1#D1.

Two conditions apply:
1. SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1 requires mTLS or a private link for C2 data in transit, which the proposal fails by using standard HTTPS. However, waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-07 waives SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1 for Parcelytics for US-only data subjects and is valid from 2026-03-01 to 2026-12-31 (covering the 2026-12-15 go-live date per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 and ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.4). Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.2, this becomes a condition.
2. CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1 applies because the planned production go-live date of 2026-12-15 falls within the Peak season freeze window (2026-12-14 to 2027-01-04). Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.3 and CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1, the go-live date must move outside the freeze window as a condition of approval.

The proposal involves delivery addresses, classified as C2 Confidential data under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 and DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1, for data subjects located in both the US and the EU. The proposal fails three rules: (1) In-transit security uses standard HTTPS instead of mTLS or private link, failing SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1. While waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-07 waives SP-3.1 for Parcelytics, it is explicitly scoped to integrations where data subjects are all in the US; because EU subjects are included, the scope limit is not met and the waiver does not apply pursuant to ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3, making this a violation under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.1. (2) Under DRS-01@v1#DR-1, C2 data about EU data subjects may only be processed and stored by vendors whose contracted hosting region is the EU; Parcelytics is contracted in the US under CT-PARCEL@v2, violating DR-1. (3) Under AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1, which supersedes the global policy for EU data subjects pursuant to ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.2, vendor retention of C2 data is capped at 14 days; Parcelytics' planned 20-day retention violates AX-EU-1. In accordance with ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, when a proposal has at least one violation, the decision must be reject and no conditions are listed.

Proposal T03 involves sending delivery addresses, which are classified as C2 Confidential personal data under DCS-01@v2 (DC-2.2 and Section 3). The proposal violates three rules:

1. SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1: C2 data leaving the internal network must use mutual TLS (mTLS) or a private link connection; standard HTTPS is insufficient. Exception register waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-07 does not apply because its scope is explicitly limited to integrations whose data subjects are all in the US, whereas this proposal includes EU data subjects (failing ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3).
2. AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1: Under the EU regional annex, vendors may retain C2 or higher data about EU data subjects for at most 14 days. The proposal specifies a 20-day retention period at Parcelytics. Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.2, this stricter regional rule replaces the global policy for EU data subjects, and no waiver applies.
3. DRS-01@v1#DR-1: C2 or higher data about EU data subjects may only be processed and stored by vendors whose contracted hosting region is the EU. Per CT-PARCEL@v2, Parcelytics' contracted hosting region is the United States.

Because there is at least one violation, under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4 the proposal must be rejected and no conditions are listed.

Delivery addresses are classified as C2 Confidential data (DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2, DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1), concerning both US and EU data subjects. While Parcelytics is eligible to receive C2 data under its DPA (SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1, CT-PARCEL@v2), the integration routes properly through int-gw from Z2 (NET-STD@v2#NZ-1, ADR-031@v1#D1), data is encrypted at rest (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2), and the 2026-11-05 go-live date avoids the change freeze (CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1, ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.4), the proposal fails three requirements:

1. Transit security (SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1): C2 data is sent over standard HTTPS instead of mTLS or a private link. Waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-07 does not apply because its scope is restricted to integrations whose data subjects are all in the US, whereas this proposal includes EU data subjects (ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3).
2. EU data retention (AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1): Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.2, the stricter EU annex replaces SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1 for EU data subjects, limiting retention to 14 days. The proposed 20-day retention violates AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1 (and no waiver applies per AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-2).
3. Data residency (DRS-01@v1#DR-1): C2 data about EU data subjects may only be processed and stored by vendors whose contracted hosting region is the EU. Under CT-PARCEL@v2, Parcelytics' contracted hosting region is the US, violating DRS-01@v1#DR-1.

Because there are unwaived violations, the proposal is rejected under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.1 and ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4.

Delivery addresses are classified as C2 Confidential personal data (DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2, DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1). Under CT-PARCEL@v2, Parcelytics is approved to process C1 and C2 data (satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1), and the sending service in Z2 properly routes traffic through int-gw (satisfying NET-STD@v2#NZ-1 and ADR-031@v1#D1; NET-STD@v2#NZ-2 applies only to Z3). Encryption at rest is also satisfied (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2), and the 2026-11-05 go-live date is outside the change freeze window (CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1). However, the proposal has three violations: (1) SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1 is violated because C2 data is sent over standard HTTPS rather than mTLS or a private link, and waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-07 does not apply under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 because its scope is restricted to integrations whose data subjects are all in the US, whereas this proposal includes EU data subjects; (2) AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1 (which replaces SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1 for EU data subjects under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.2) is violated because C2 data about EU data subjects is retained for 20 days, exceeding the 14-day maximum; and (3) DRS-01@v1#DR-1 is violated because C2 data about EU data subjects is sent to Parcelytics, whose contracted hosting region under CT-PARCEL@v2 is the United States rather than the EU. In accordance with ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, the proposal is rejected.

The integration transmits C2 personal data (customer phone numbers) to InsightHub via int-gw with mutual TLS, meeting SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1, NET-STD@v2#NZ-1, and ADR-031@v1#D1. The vendor's contract (CT-INSIGHT@v1) covers C2 data and permits processing US data subjects in the EU under DRS-01@v1#DR-2. The proposed 50-day data retention exceeds the 30-day limit set by SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1; however, this is covered by waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-12 (valid until 2026-11-30, permitting up to 60 days retention for InsightHub). Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.2, this is approved with conditions, subject to the vendor maintaining retention at or below 60 days and the waiver remaining valid through the go live date.

The vendor agreement CT-INSIGHT@v1 covers C1 and C2 data (satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1), transit uses mutual TLS (satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1), and data is encrypted at rest (satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2). The data subjects reside in the US, permitting processing in InsightHub's contracted EU hosting region under DRS-01@v1#DR-2, and rendering AX-EU@v1 inapplicable. Network routing from Zone Z2 via int-gw complies with NET-STD@v2#NZ-1 and ADR-031@v1#D1 (egress proxy under NZ-2 applies only to Z3). The planned go-live date of 2026-11-19 falls outside the peak season change freeze under CHG-CAL@2026.

However, InsightHub's planned 50-day data retention exceeds the 30-day limit set by SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1. This is covered by waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-12, which permits InsightHub retention up to 60 days and is valid through 2026-11-30. Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.2, SP-4.1 becomes an approved condition rather than a violation. Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, because there are zero violations and one condition, the proposal is approved with conditions.

The integration transmits driver location (Class C2 personal data under DCS-01@v2) and route plans (Class C1) to RouteMind. Under CT-ROUTE@v1, RouteMind's DPA covers C2 data and its contracted hosting region is APAC (Singapore), satisfying DRS-01@v1#DR-2. The sending service is in network zone Z2 and routes outbound traffic via int-gw using mTLS, satisfying NET-STD@v2#NZ-1, ADR-031@v1#D1, and SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1. RouteMind retains data for 10 days, complying with SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1.

While RouteMind stores data unencrypted at rest (failing SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2), this is covered by waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-15, which specifically names RouteMind and SP-4.2 and is valid from 2026-06-01 to 2027-03-31 (encompassing the planned 2026-11-18 go-live date). Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.2, this is approved with conditions: Northwind must implement the compensating control specified in W-15 (replacing customer and driver names and IDs with pseudonyms prior to sending), and the integration may proceed only while W-15 remains valid.

Data subjects are in APAC and RouteMind's contracted hosting region in CT-ROUTE@v1 is APAC (Singapore), which complies with DRS-01@v1#DR-2. AX-EU@v1 does not apply as there are no EU data subjects.

The proposal must be rejected due to two policy violations for which no waivers exist in EXC-REG@2026-10:

1. SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1: The proposal includes sending customer email addresses, which are C2 Confidential personal data under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 (and thus the integration takes class C2 under DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1). Under SP-2.1, a vendor may receive data only up to the highest class covered by its Data Processing Agreement (DPA). TrackWave's agreement (CT-TRACK@v1) covers C1 data only and explicitly states TrackWave is not approved to receive personal data.

2. NET-STD@v2#NZ-2: The sending service is hosted in network zone Z3. Under NZ-2, any outbound connection from a service in Z3 to an external destination must pass through the egress proxy, but the proposal explicitly specifies that outbound traffic does not use the egress proxy.

Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, a proposal with at least one violation must be rejected with no conditions listed.

The proposal fails on two separate mandatory requirements and must be rejected pursuant to ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4:

1. Vendor DPA Eligibility (SP-2.1): The proposal includes sending customer email addresses alongside vehicle telemetry. Under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2, customer email addresses are classified as C2 (Confidential) personal data, which elevates the entire integration to Class C2 under DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1. However, under vendor contract CT-TRACK@v1, TrackWave's Data Processing Agreement (DPA) covers C1 data only and expressly stipulates that TrackWave is not approved to receive personal data. Sending C2 data to TrackWave therefore violates SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1. No waiver exists in EXC-REG@2026-10 for this rule or vendor.

2. Network Egress Proxy (NZ-2): The sending service operates in high-security network zone Z3. Under NET-STD@v2#NZ-2, any outbound connection from a service in Z3 to an external destination must pass through the egress proxy. The proposal explicitly specifies that outbound traffic does not use the egress proxy, violating NET-STD@v2#NZ-2. There is no active waiver in effect for this integration (historical waiver W-03 expired on 2026-02-28).

In accordance with ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, because there are violations, the proposal is rejected and no conditions are listed.

The proposal includes customer email addresses, which are classified as C2 data under DCS-01@v2. Under CT-TRACK@v1, TrackWave's data processing agreement covers C1 data only, so sending C2 data violates SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1. Furthermore, the sending service runs in network zone Z3 and sends outbound traffic to an external destination without passing through the egress proxy, violating NET-STD@v2#NZ-2 (waiver W-03 expired on 2026-02-28, prior to the planned 2026-11-24 go-live date, and does not apply). Because there are unwaived violations, the proposal is rejected.

Under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 and DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1, the integration is classified as C2 because it includes customer email addresses alongside C1 vehicle telemetry. Evaluating the proposal against all applicable current standards yields two unwaived violations:

1. Vendor eligibility (SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1): TrackWave's agreement (CT-TRACK@v1) states that its data processing agreement covers C1 data only and TrackWave is not approved to receive personal data. Sending C2 customer email addresses to TrackWave violates SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1, and no waiver in EXC-REG@2026-10 covers this rule.
2. Network egress (NET-STD@v2#NZ-2): The sending service runs in high-security zone Z3, where any outbound connection to an external destination must pass through the egress proxy. Because outbound traffic does not use the egress proxy, the proposal violates NET-STD@v2#NZ-2. Waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-03 does not apply under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 and ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.4 because it expired on 2026-02-28 (prior to the 2026-11-24 planned go-live date) and does not name TrackWave.

All other rules are satisfied: data in transit uses mTLS (SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1), retention is 7 days (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1), data is encrypted at rest (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2), US data subject residency in the US is permitted (DRS-01@v1#DR-2), traffic routes through int-gw (ADR-031@v1#D1), and the 2026-11-24 go-live date is outside the CHG-CAL@2026 freeze window. Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, the proposal is rejected.

Proposal T07 transmits vehicle telemetry and route plans, both of which are classified as C1 Internal data under DCS-01@v2. Under CT-TRACK@v1, TrackWave's Data Processing Agreement covers C1 data, satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1. C1 data may use standard HTTPS (SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.2), has no retention or encryption at rest mandates under SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.3, and has no data residency restrictions under DRS-01@v1#DR-3 (meaning AX-EU@v1 and DRS-01@v1#DR-1 do not apply). The sending service resides in zone Z2 and routes outbound vendor calls via int-gw, adhering to NET-STD@v2#NZ-1 and ADR-031@v1#D1. Finally, the planned production go-live of 2027-01-05 falls after the peak season freeze window ending 2027-01-04 (CHG-CAL@2026). With no violations and no conditions, the proposal is approved.

Proposal T07 is approved with no violations and no conditions. Under DCS-01@v2 (Section 3 and DC-3.1), vehicle telemetry and route plans are classified as C1 (Internal operational data). TrackWave's master services agreement (CT-TRACK@v1) includes a Data Processing Agreement covering C1 data, satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1. In-transit transfer over standard HTTPS complies with SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.2. Because the data is C1, retention of 365 days and unencrypted storage at rest comply with SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.3; neither AX-EU@v1 (which applies only to C2 or higher data) nor DRS-01@v1 (under DR-3, C1 has no residency restrictions) imposes restrictions. Network egress from zone Z2 via int-gw complies with NET-STD@v2#NZ-1 and ADR-031@v1#D1, and the egress proxy is not required as the service is not in Z3 (NET-STD@v2#NZ-2). Finally, the planned go-live date of 2027-01-05 falls outside the Peak Season change freeze window (2026-12-14 to 2027-01-04 under CHG-CAL@2026), so no change freeze condition applies under CF-1.

Proposal T07 sends only vehicle telemetry and route plans, both of which are classified as C1 Internal data under DCS-01@v2 (overall classification C1 per DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1). TrackWave's DPA in CT-TRACK@v1 covers C1 data, satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1. Because the integration involves only C1 data, standard HTTPS is permitted (SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.2), there are no retention or encryption-at-rest requirements (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.3), the EU regional annex does not apply (AX-EU@v1), and there are no data residency restrictions (DRS-01@v1#DR-3). The sending service in network zone Z2 routes outbound traffic through the integration gateway (int-gw), complying with NET-STD@v2#NZ-1 and ADR-031@v1#D1 (the egress proxy rule NET-STD@v2#NZ-2 applies only to Z3). Finally, the planned go-live date of 2027-01-05 falls outside the peak season change freeze window ending 2027-01-04 (CHG-CAL@2026). With no violations and no conditions, the proposal is approved under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4.

Under DCS-01@v2 (DC-2.1, DC-3.1), both vehicle telemetry (not joined with a driver roster) and route plans are classified as C1 Internal data, making the overall integration data class C1. Evaluating all applicable rules against C1 data:

1. Vendor eligibility (SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1, SP-2.2): TrackWave's contract (CT-TRACK@v1) covers C1 data under its DPA, and no C3 data is sent.
2. Data in transit (SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.2): Standard HTTPS (server-side TLS) is permitted for C1 data.
3. Data at rest and retention (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.3, AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1): C1 data has no retention or encryption-at-rest requirement under SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.3 (365-day retention and unencrypted storage at rest are permitted), and AX-EU@v1 applies only to personal data (C2 or higher).
4. Data residency (DRS-01@v1#DR-3): C1 data has no residency restriction, regardless of whether people associated with operations are in the US or the EU.
5. Network zoning and integration gateway (NET-STD@v2#NZ-1, NZ-2; ADR-031@v1#D1): The sending service runs in zone Z2 and routes traffic through the integration gateway (int-gw). The egress proxy requirement (NET-STD@v2#NZ-2) applies only to zone Z3.
6. Change calendar (CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1): The planned production go-live date of 2027-01-05 falls after the peak season freeze window (2026-12-14 to 2027-01-04 inclusive).

Because there are no violations and no conditions, the proposal is approved under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4.

The proposal must be rejected due to three rule violations: (1) Under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.3 and DC-3.1, card numbers (PAN) are Class C3 (Restricted) data. Under SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.2, C3 data must never be sent to a third party. (2) Parcelytics' Data Processing Agreement under CT-PARCEL@v2 covers only C1 and C2 data and explicitly excludes C3 data, violating SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1. (3) The service calls the vendor's API directly from its own code rather than routing outbound vendor traffic through the integration gateway int-gw, violating ADR-031@v1#D1. In accordance with ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, when a proposal is rejected, all violations are listed and no conditions are recorded.

Under DCS-01@v2 (DC-2.3 and DC-3.1), card numbers (PAN) are classified as C3 Restricted data, meaning the integration payload is classified as C3. The proposal fails three rules: (1) Under SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1, a vendor may only receive data up to the highest class covered by its DPA. Under contract CT-PARCEL@v2, Parcelytics' DPA covers only C1 and C2 data, explicitly excluding C3 data. (2) Under SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.2, C3 data must never be sent to a third party under any circumstances and card numbers must be tokenized by the payments platform before data leaves Northwind. (3) Under ADR-031@v1#D1, all outbound integrations to external vendors must route through the integration gateway (int-gw); services are prohibited from calling vendor APIs directly from service code. No applicable waiver in EXC-REG@2026-10 covers these rules. Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, a proposal with at least one violation must be rejected with no conditions listed.

Proposal T08 sends card numbers (PAN), which are classified as C3 Restricted data under DCS-01@v2 (DC-2.3, DC-3.1). This results in three unwaived violations: (1) SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1 is violated because Parcelytics' data processing agreement in CT-PARCEL@v2 only covers C1 and C2 data and explicitly excludes C3 data; (2) SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.2 is violated because C3 data may never be sent to a third party and card numbers must be tokenized before leaving Northwind; and (3) ADR-031@v1#D1 is violated because the service calls the vendor's API directly rather than routing through the integration gateway (int-gw). Because there is at least one violation, the proposal is rejected.

Under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.3 and DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1, the integration is classified as C3 (Restricted) because it includes card numbers (PAN) alongside C1 shipment IDs. Evaluating all applicable rules in the review pack against Proposal T08 yields three unwaived violations:

1. SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1: A vendor may receive data only up to the highest class covered by its data processing agreement (DPA). Under CT-PARCEL@v2, Parcelytics's DPA covers only C1 and C2 data and explicitly excludes C3 data.
2. SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.2: C3 data must never be sent to a third party regardless of its DPA; card numbers must be tokenized by the payments platform before leaving Northwind.
3. ADR-031@v1#D1: Every integration sending data to an external vendor must route through the integration gateway (int-gw), and services must not call vendor APIs directly. Although the Z3 service passes traffic through the egress proxy in compliance with NET-STD@v2#NZ-2, it calls the vendor's API directly from its own code rather than routing through int-gw.

Other requirements are satisfied: mutual TLS satisfies SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1, the 5-day retention period satisfies SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1, encryption at rest satisfies SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2, US data residency with US subjects satisfies DRS-01@v1#DR-2, and the 2026-11-30 go-live date is outside the CHG-CAL@2026 freeze window. Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, because there is at least one violation, the proposal is rejected.

Customer email addresses constitute C2 Confidential personal data under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2. The proposal sends personal data concerning EU data subjects to InsightHub with a vendor retention period of 55 days. Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.2, AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1 supersedes the global retention policy for EU data subjects and restricts retention of C2 or higher data to at most 14 days. While waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-12 permits InsightHub to retain data up to 60 days against SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1, per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 and AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-2 a global waiver does not name or cover regional annex rules, and no exception to AX-EU-1 is in effect. Because the 55-day retention period fails AX-EU-1 with no applicable waiver, this constitutes a violation under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.1. Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, a proposal with at least one violation must be rejected with no conditions listed.

Customer email addresses are classified as C2 Confidential personal data under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 and DC-3.1. Under AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1, vendors may retain C2 or higher data about EU data subjects for at most 14 days after receipt. The proposal specifies a 55-day retention period by InsightHub for data that includes EU data subjects, which exceeds this 14-day limit. Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.2, regional annex AX-EU@v1 sets a stricter requirement than SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1 and replaces the global policy for EU data subjects. Although waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-12 permits InsightHub to retain data for up to 60 days under SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1, it waives only SP-4.1; under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 and AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-2, waivers granted against the global security policy do not waive AX-EU, and a waiver never covers a rule it does not name. Because no valid waiver covers AX-EU-1, this failure constitutes a violation under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.1. Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, the presence of at least one violation requires that the proposal be rejected and that no conditions be listed.

Proposal T09 sends customer email addresses, which are classified as C2 Confidential data under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 and DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1, to InsightHub for data subjects located in both the EU and the US. InsightHub's contract (CT-INSIGHT@v1) covers C1 and C2 data and provides EU hosting, satisfying vendor eligibility (SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1) and EU data residency (DRS-01@v1#DR-1, DRS-01@v1#DR-2). Network routing through int-gw from Z2, use of a private link connection, and encryption at rest satisfy ADR-031@v1#D1, NET-STD@v2#NZ-1, SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1, and SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2. The planned go-live of 2026-11-12 falls outside the change freeze window in CHG-CAL@2026. For the US data subjects, the global 30-day retention limit (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1) applies per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.2, and the proposed 55-day retention is covered by waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-12 (which allows InsightHub up to 60 days retention through 2026-11-30). However, for the EU data subjects, AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1 sets a stricter 14-day maximum retention limit that replaces the global requirement under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.2. Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 and AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-2, waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-12 waives only SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1 and does not waive AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1, and no DPO exception is in force. Because retaining EU C2 data for 55 days violates AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1 without an applicable waiver, the proposal must be rejected under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.1 and ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, with no conditions listed.

Under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 and DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1, customer email addresses are classified as C2 Confidential data. Per CT-INSIGHT@v1, InsightHub's DPA covers C1 and C2 data (satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1) and its contracted hosting region is the EU (satisfying DRS-01@v1#DR-1 for EU data subjects and DRS-01@v1#DR-2 for US data subjects). The integration uses a private link connection (satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1), stores data encrypted at rest (satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2), and routes traffic from network zone Z2 through int-gw without requiring the Z3 egress proxy (satisfying NET-STD@v2#NZ-1, NET-STD@v2#NZ-2, and ADR-031@v1#D1). The planned go-live date of 2026-11-12 is outside the peak season change freeze window (CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1).

However, the proposal retains C2 data about both EU and US data subjects for 55 days. Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.2, US data subjects remain under the global 30-day retention limit in SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1, which is covered by waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-12 (valid through 2026-11-30 for InsightHub up to 60 days). For EU data subjects, the stricter 14-day retention limit in AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1 replaces SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1. Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 and AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-2, EXC-REG@2026-10#W-12 only waives SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1 and does not waive AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1. Retaining EU C2 data for 55 days is therefore an unwaived violation of AX-EU@v1#AX-EU-1 (ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.1). In accordance with ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, the proposal is rejected and no conditions are listed.

The integration transmits C2 personal data (delivery addresses) to RouteMind. Under SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2, C2 data must be stored encrypted at rest, which RouteMind does not support per CT-ROUTE@v1. However, waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-15 applies through 2027-03-31, converting SP-4.2 into a condition requiring Northwind to pseudonymise customer and driver names and IDs before sending. Additionally, the planned go-live date of 2027-01-04 falls on the final day of the peak season freeze window (2026-12-14 through 2027-01-04 inclusive), which is recorded as a condition under CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1 requiring the go-live to move outside the freeze window. With no unexcused violations, the proposal is approved with conditions.

The integration transmits delivery addresses (C2 Confidential) and route plans (C1 Internal), classifying the integration overall as C2 under DCS-01@v2. RouteMind is contracted to process C1 and C2 data (CT-ROUTE@v1) satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1, and data subjects are in APAC satisfying DRS-01@v1#DR-2. Transit via private link satisfies SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1, retention of 14 days satisfies SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1, and routing through the Z3 egress proxy and int-gw satisfies NET-STD@v2#NZ-2 and ADR-031@v1#D1.

Two conditions apply:
1. SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2: RouteMind does not encrypt data at rest. However, waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-15 covers SP-4.2 for RouteMind through 2027-03-31, which encompasses the planned go-live date. Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 and CH-3.2, this is approved as a condition provided Northwind applies the compensating control (replacing customer and driver names and IDs with pseudonyms prior to transmission) while the waiver remains valid.
2. CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1: The planned go-live date of 2027-01-04 falls on the final inclusive day of the Peak Season freeze window (2026-12-14 through 2027-01-04). Under CF-1 and ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.3, production go-live is approved only on the condition that the date is rescheduled outside the freeze window.

Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, because there are zero violations and at least one condition, the proposal is approved with conditions.

The integration sends delivery addresses (C2) and route plans (C1), classifying the overall payload as C2 Confidential. RouteMind's contract (CT-ROUTE@v1) covers C1 and C2 data under its DPA and hosts data in APAC (Singapore), satisfying vendor eligibility (SP-2.1) and data residency for APAC data subjects (DR-2). Network egress from Z3 passes through the egress proxy (NZ-2), routes through the integration gateway int-gw (ADR-031@v1#D1), uses a private link connection (SP-3.1), and retains data for 14 days (within the 30-day limit of SP-4.1). However, RouteMind stores the data without encryption at rest, which fails SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2. Because waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-15 covers SP-4.2 for RouteMind through 2027-03-31 (encompassing the 2027-01-04 go-live date), this becomes a condition requiring the waiver's compensating control (pseudonymising customer and driver names and IDs before sending) to be in place while the waiver remains valid. Additionally, the planned production go-live date of 2027-01-04 falls on the final inclusive day of the peak season freeze window (2026-12-14 to 2027-01-04), creating a second condition under CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1 that the go-live date move outside the freeze window.

1. Data Classification (DCS-01@v2): The integration sends route plans (C1 under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.1) and delivery addresses (C2 under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2). Under DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1, the integration is classified as C2.

2. Vendor Eligibility & Residency (SEC-POL@v3, DRS-01@v1, CT-ROUTE@v1): Under CT-ROUTE@v1, RouteMind's DPA covers C1 and C2 data and its contracted hosting region is APAC (Singapore). This satisfies SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1 and SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.2 (no C3 data is sent). Because all data subjects are in APAC, AX-EU@v1 does not apply, and processing in RouteMind's contracted APAC region complies with DRS-01@v1#DR-2.

3. Data in Transit & Network Egress (SEC-POL@v3, NET-STD@v2, ADR-031@v1): Data is transferred over a private link connection, satisfying SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1. Outbound traffic from the Z3 service passes through the egress proxy (satisfying NET-STD@v2#NZ-2) and routes through the integration gateway int-gw (satisfying ADR-031@v1#D1).

4. Data at Rest & Retention (SEC-POL@v3, EXC-REG@2026-10): RouteMind retains the data for 14 days, meeting the 30-day maximum in SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1. However, RouteMind stores the data without encryption at rest (CT-ROUTE@v1), failing SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2. Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 and CH-3.2, waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-15 covers SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2 for vendor RouteMind on the planned go-live date of 2027-01-04 (within the waiver's 2026-06-01 to 2027-03-31 validity period). Therefore, SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2 is recorded as a condition requiring that the waiver remain valid and its compensating control (replacing customer and driver names and IDs with pseudonyms before sending) be in place.

5. Change Calendar (CHG-CAL@2026): Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.4 and CH-3.3, the planned production go-live date of 2027-01-04 falls within the Peak season freeze window (2026-12-14 to 2027-01-04, inclusive). Under CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1, this is recorded as a condition requiring that the production go-live move outside the freeze window.

6. Decision (ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4): With no violations and two conditions (SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2 and CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1), the proposal is approved with conditions.

The integration transmits customer email addresses and delivery addresses, which are classified as C2 Confidential data under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 and DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1. Under SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1, C2 or higher data leaving the internal network must use mutual TLS (mTLS) or a private link connection; standard HTTPS is insufficient. While waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-07 permits standard HTTPS for Parcelytics for US data subjects, ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 and ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.4 dictate that waiver validity is evaluated against the planned go live date (2027-01-15). Because W-07 expired on 2026-12-31, it does not apply. Consequently, the proposal fails SP-3.1 without an applicable waiver, constituting a violation under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.1. Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, proposals with at least one violation must be rejected with no conditions listed.

Proposal T11 involves sending customer email addresses and delivery addresses to Parcelytics. Under DCS-01@v2 Section 3 and DC-3.1, both elements are classified as C2 Confidential (personal data), making the overall integration C2. Under SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1, any C2 or higher data leaving the internal network must use mutual TLS (mTLS) or a private link connection; standard HTTPS with server-side TLS alone is not permitted. The proposal specifies transferring data over standard HTTPS, which fails SP-3.1. While exception register EXC-REG@2026-10 contains waiver W-07 waiving SP-3.1 for Parcelytics for US data subjects, ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 and CH-2.4 dictate that waiver validity must be judged against the proposal's planned production go-live date of 2027-01-15. Waiver W-07 expired on 2026-12-31 and is therefore not valid on the go-live date. Because the proposal fails SP-3.1 and no applicable waiver covers it, SP-3.1 constitutes a violation under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.1. Pursuant to ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, the existence of at least one violation requires a decision of reject, with all violations listed and no conditions listed.

Under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 and DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1, customer email addresses and delivery addresses classify the integration data as C2 Confidential. Under the current security policy (SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1, applicable per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.1), C2 data leaving the internal network must use mutual TLS (mTLS) or a private link connection; standard HTTPS (server-side TLS) is not sufficient. The proposal uses standard HTTPS. Although waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-07 waives SP-3.1 for Parcelytics for US data subjects, its validity period ends on 2026-12-31. Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 and ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.4, waiver validity is judged against the planned go-live date of 2027-01-15, making W-07 inapplicable. All other requirements (vendor eligibility under CT-PARCEL@v2, US data residency, 30-day retention, encryption at rest, routing from Z2 via int-gw, and go-live outside the change freeze window) are satisfied. Because SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1 is failed without an applicable waiver, it is a violation (ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.1), requiring rejection (ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4).

Under DCS-01@v2#DC-2.2 and DCS-01@v2#DC-3.1, customer email addresses and delivery addresses classify the integration as C2 Confidential. Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.1, SEC-POL@v3 is the current security policy and supersedes SEC-POL@v2. Sending C2 data over standard HTTPS (server-side TLS) fails SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1, which requires mutual TLS (mTLS) or a private link connection for C2 or higher data. Although waiver EXC-REG@2026-10#W-07 waives SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1 for Parcelytics integrations involving US data subjects, its validity period is 2026-03-01 to 2026-12-31. Under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.3 and ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-2.4, waiver validity is judged against the planned production go-live date of 2027-01-15, which falls after the waiver expires; therefore, EXC-REG@2026-10#W-07 does not apply and SEC-POL@v3#SP-3.1 is an unwaived violation under ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.1. All other applicable rules are satisfied: CT-PARCEL@v2 covers C1 and C2 data under its DPA (SEC-POL@v3#SP-2.1) and provides US hosting for US data subjects (DRS-01@v1#DR-2; AX-EU@v1 does not apply); the 30-day retention and encryption at rest meet SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.1 and SEC-POL@v3#SP-4.2; routing from network zone Z2 via int-gw without the Z3 egress proxy satisfies NET-STD@v2#NZ-1, NET-STD@v2#NZ-2, and ADR-031@v1#D1; and the 2027-01-15 go-live date is outside the CHG-CAL@2026#CF-1 freeze window (2026-12-14 to 2027-01-04). Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, the proposal is rejected.

Driver location is classified as C2 confidential personal data under DCS-01@v2. The proposal involves sending data about EU data subjects to RouteMind. Under DRS-01@v1#DR-1, C2 or higher data concerning EU data subjects may only be processed and stored by vendors whose contracted hosting region is the EU. According to CT-ROUTE@v1, RouteMind's contracted hosting region is Asia Pacific (APAC), Singapore. This constitutes a violation of DR-1, which cannot be waived. Per ARB-CHARTER@v1#CH-3.4, the presence of at least one violation requires a rejection with no conditions listed.
